key_insight: Reinterpreting exponential shear through evolving kinematic and stress eigenvalues and eigenvectors enables one test to recover both the steady shear flow curve and the steady planar extensional viscosity curve.
engineering_relevance: The approach could simplify complex-fluid characterization by measuring shear and planar extensional responses using commercial strain-controlled rheometers.
method: Impose exponentially increasing shear deformation and measure time-varying torque and normal force.
Analyze the evolving eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the deformation kinematics and sample stress.
Define material functions that map the transient measurements to steady shear and planar extensional viscosity curves.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports support from simulations of multiple nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive models, asymptotic analysis, and experiments with several polymeric liquids.
watch_item: Implementation requires accurate transient torque and normal-force measurements; applicability beyond the tested polymeric liquids remains to be established.
paper_title: A new approach to measuring both the steady flow curve and the planar extensional viscosity of complex fluids using exponential shear
